slides.title: Languages and Communication
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 1: Languages and Communication. The theme is languages and communication: how ideas travel, how rumours outrun facts, and how careful readers and listeners separate the two. You will read two information texts about how rumours spread and how to check them, then follow Amal and Nora through the story Whispers Beyond the Gate as a hoax flyer sweeps their harbour city. The grammar focus covers contrast conjunctions (although, while, whereas), -ing forms as subjects and objects, the present continuous, abstract nouns, reported speech, conditionals, connectives and multi-word verbs. Along the way you will learn thirty-one new words, write a contrast paragraph and an opinion essay, and argue a case aloud for five to six minutes. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Summarise the central ideas and important details in Languages and Communication texts.
Support inferences and comparisons with relevant text evidence.
Use Grade 8 vocabulary accurately in discussion and writing.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to summarise the central ideas and important details in Languages and Communication texts. You will also support inferences and comparisons with relevant text evidence. You will also use Grade 8 vocabulary accurately in discussion and writing. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: abstraction, accessibility, assimilation, semantic-field, structuralism, textual-analysis. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: The Speed of a Whisper: How Rumours Travel
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Speed of a Whisper: How Rumours Travel and The Fact-Checker's Toolkit. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Contrast Conjunctions: Although, While and Whereas
bullets: Although, while and whereas are contrast conjunctions: they join two clauses that express different or surprising ideas, showing that both things can be...
slides.narration: The first language focus is Contrast Conjunctions: Although, While and Whereas. Although, while and whereas are contrast conjunctions: they join two clauses that express different or surprising ideas, showing that both things can be true at the same time even when they seem to conflict. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: Opinion Essay on Spotting Misinformation
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Contrast Debate. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
